requirements.requirement: Existing museum validator zero errors and citation check zero failures
requirements.evidenceSoFar: npm run validate on branch claude/islam-museum-gaming-v2-c9bd91, 25 Nov 2026: 0 errors (89,037 entities, 254,481 prose files, 7,674 warnings, 4 min 48 s). No museum content changed, so the citation check has nothing to check yet. Re-run on every gaming pull request.

requirements.requirement: Complete playable scoped loop and campaign or challenges, failure/recovery
requirements.evidence: real browser playthrough recording and test
requirements.evidenceSoFar: Two prototypes. Atlas: a full five-round daily game played in real Chrome 158 by script in seven languages, docs/gaming/evidence/m2/atlas/. The Golden Age: the campaign's three chapters, played by script in real Chrome 158 in seven languages (mouse, keyboard alone, plan view, without 3D), and each chapter's whole campaign driven through the screen in English and Arabic (the first and third to a win, the second to its end short of the goal on that seed); the third chapter has a dominant strategy, recorded in docs/gaming/games/golden-age.md; with the loss conditions and their visible count under unit test; docs/gaming/evidence/m2/golden-age/screen/. No recording and no human playthrough of either. The other eight games do not exist.

requirements.requirement: Save, reload, migration and corruption recovery
requirements.evidenceSoFar: Atlas: save round trip, unreadable save set aside, newer save not overwritten, damaged entry dropped, game from another pack not resumed (unit tests), reload in mid-game and corrupted save (browser script). The Golden Age: the same cases, plus a state the rules could not have produced is refused (unit tests), reload in mid-game and corrupted save (browser script). The Golden Age's save format has one migration (version 1 to 2, when endowments were added), with a unit test that a migrated game plays on exactly as before; Atlas has only one save version. Saves are in localStorage, not yet the IndexedDB envelope of specification 06.

requirements.evidence: solver output, dataset digest, UTC fixtures
requirements.evidenceSoFar: Atlas: all 365 scheduled days checked valid by the unit tests on the pinned pack (digest 764f347c…f69ae): five different places a day, no round twice, UTC fixtures over month ends and leap days. "Solvable" here means every round has one recorded place with site or locality coordinates; no solver is needed. Other daily games do not exist.

requirements.requirement: Historical facts and asset rights verified
requirements.evidence: record IDs, citation and license audit
requirements.evidenceSoFar: Atlas: every round is a museum record id joined to a museum place id; no image or third-party asset is used; coastlines are Natural Earth via world-atlas (public domain). The Golden Age: its district, numbers and buildings are fiction and say so; research and tools link to thirteen museum records by id from a pinned file (docs/gaming/games/golden-age.md), chosen by an agent and not yet checked by the founder; no third-party asset is used. Music in both: the museum's own suite, described in the Backstage page's words (docs/gaming/adr/G-0007-music-and-audio.md). No independent citation or licence audit has been done.

requirements.requirement: Seven locales and essential accessible controls
requirements.evidence: screenshots, functional tests, human language review
requirements.evidenceSoFar: Atlas: interface in all seven languages, right-to-left for Arabic and Urdu, keyboard-only play and typed coordinates, screenshots in evidence/m2/atlas/. The Golden Age: 260 strings in seven languages, panels change sides for Arabic and Urdu and the district is never mirrored, keyboard-only play, a plan view in which every plot and canal link is a labelled button and which is the whole game without WebGPU, reduced-motion respected; functional run in each language, evidence/m2/golden-age/screen/. All strings are AI-written and unreviewed by a native speaker; no screen-reader test by a person; touch untried.

requirements.requirement: Actual real GPU benchmark, soak and device loss
requirements.evidenceSoFar: One machine only: Apple M4 Max, Chrome 158. Reference district: docs/gaming/evidence/m1/. The Golden Age: frame intervals at 1920 × 1080 during a scripted campaign, with no frame over 16.7 ms after a stall at each season's end was traced and removed, docs/gaming/LEDGER.md (Measurements). No soak, no device-loss test, no Windows or discrete-GPU machine, Edge run did not start. See m1-graphics-spike.md.
